americas_summary: Current Americas exposure is being driven more by trade, energy, supply-chain, cyber, and financial transmission than by broad public disorder. Civil unrest and public order are now monitored as a dedicated domain and will rise only when violence, duration, emergency measures, or disruption to essential services materially affects civilians.
confidence_rationale: Multiple authoritative sources support the major energy, trade, shipping, and financial signals, while some downstream civilian impacts and civil-order pathways remain uncertain or uneven.
summary: Global threat conditions are severe, but broad civilian systems remain functional. The calibrated preparedness score emphasizes observed disruption, Americas exposure, persistence, and hard triggers so that high geopolitical stress does not automatically produce an imminent-disaster label.
primary_driver: Energy and maritime disruption remain the strongest near-term transmission pathway into fuel, freight, inflation, and financial stress.
primary_stabilizers: Global financial markets, payment systems, and major exchanges remain operational.
Alternative trade and maritime routes remain partially functional.
No broad Americas civil-order breakdown is currently a leading systemic driver.
Food, banking, grid, and retail systems remain broadly functional in most of the Americas.
Government, central-bank, and emergency-management mechanisms remain active.

domains.name: Energy security
domains.rationale: Energy and maritime chokepoint disruption is actively affecting oil prices, shipping risk, and downstream transport costs.

domains.name: Military / geopolitical
domains.rationale: Active interstate conflict creates substantial escalation risk, but the household score is moderated unless disruption transmits into civilian systems.

domains.name: Supply chain & transportation
domains.rationale: Shipping, insurance, rerouting, and freight pressure create credible near-term availability and price effects.

domains.name: Global trade fragmentation
domains.rationale: Tariffs, retaliation, import restrictions, and export controls are increasingly relevant to North American prices and supply chains.

domains.name: Technology chokepoints
domains.rationale: Critical-mineral and semiconductor concentration remains a meaningful disruption pathway without broad consumer shortages at present.

domains.name: Critical infrastructure / cyber
domains.rationale: Grid, telecom, payment, satellite, port, and subsea infrastructure are high-consequence targets, while widespread outages are not currently observed.

domains.name: Financial-system stress
domains.rationale: Energy inflation and higher yields are tightening conditions, while core banking and payment systems continue functioning.

domains.name: Food & agriculture
domains.rationale: Fuel, fertilizer, freight, and trade costs are increasing vulnerability without broad food shortages or rationing.

domains.name: Domestic institutional stress
domains.rationale: Policy friction and emergency measures can affect civilian access, but broad institutional failure is not evident.

domains.name: Civil unrest / public order
domains.rationale: The domain now monitors riots, violent unrest, major strikes, curfews, emergency deployments, and essential-service disruption while excluding peaceful protest from elevated scoring.

domains.name: Public health / biological
domains.rationale: No current biological event is producing pandemic-scale disruption across the Americas.

domains.name: Natural / environmental
domains.rationale: Localized natural hazards can be severe, but there is no current multi-region natural-disaster cascade driving global systemic risk.

areas_to_watch.name: Hormuz traffic and energy flows
areas_to_watch.why: A sustained physical reduction in tanker or LNG movement could convert price stress into availability constraints.

areas_to_watch.name: U.S.–Canada and wider trade retaliation
areas_to_watch.why: Expansion into energy, food, metals, vehicles, agricultural inputs, or critical goods could increase Americas exposure quickly.

areas_to_watch.name: Americas civil unrest and major strikes
areas_to_watch.why: Watch for sustained violence, curfews, emergency deployments, or port, rail, trucking, border, fuel, or essential-service disruption.

areas_to_watch.name: Cyber incidents affecting utilities or payments
areas_to_watch.why: A confirmed prolonged outage affecting power, water, telecom, ports, payments, GPS, or banking would rapidly raise observed disruption.

areas_to_watch.name: Financial stress and credit conditions
areas_to_watch.why: Persistent inflation, funding stress, bank-access restrictions, or payment disruptions could amplify other supply shocks.

areas_to_watch.name: Food, fertilizer, and freight restrictions
areas_to_watch.why: Export restrictions or supply interruptions could transmit energy and trade stress into household essentials.

signals.title: Critical subsea infrastructure remains under heightened scrutiny
signals.summary: Undersea communications and energy infrastructure remain high-consequence targets, but broad service failure is not currently observed.

signals.title: Global financial plumbing remains functional despite energy shock
signals.summary: Market stress and higher yields are meaningful, but core banking, payments, and exchange operations remain functioning.

preparedness_actions: Complete sensible, previously planned preparedness purchases while normal supply channels are functioning.
Maintain several weeks of food, household consumables, water capacity, and essential medical supplies.
Keep vehicles reasonably fueled and verify generator, battery, solar, or other backup-power capability.
Maintain diversified payment options and a reasonable amount of emergency cash.
Confirm family communications, transportation, and meeting plans.
Avoid panic buying; focus on resilience gaps that would be difficult to correct after disruption begins.
historical_note: Illustrative reference markers only. They are not used in the live score until formal back-testing is completed.

methodology.note: All-hazards early-warning assessment. The score is a preparedness-urgency index, not the probability that a disaster, collapse, or war will occur.
methodology.formula: Preparedness Urgency = 40% Global Threat Pressure + 25% Observed Civilian Disruption + 10% Cross-System Coupling + 10% Momentum/Persistence + 15% Americas Exposure. Global threat, observed impact, and Americas exposure are weighted averages across all 12 domains.
methodology.rate_limits: Absent a verified hard trigger, normal daily movement is limited to ±3 points. A verified but non-severe hard trigger allows up to ±6. A verified national, multinational, or global hard trigger can bypass the rate limit.
methodology.stage_guardrails: HIGH ALERT begins at 80. IMMINENT DISRUPTION requires a score of at least 90, observed disruption of at least 75, and a verified severe hard trigger plus either 48-hour persistence or an active fast-onset trigger. ACTIVE DISRUPTION requires at least 97, observed disruption at least 85, three high-impact domains, and two verified severe triggers.
methodology.civil_unrest: Civil Unrest / Public Order is scored from observable violence, duration, geographic spread, emergency measures, infrastructure damage, and disruption to transport, commerce, public safety, or essential services. Peaceful protest and political ideology do not raise the score by themselves.
methodology.confidence: Evidence confidence is displayed separately and does not increase preparedness urgency.
methodology.domains: Military/geopolitical, energy, trade, supply chain/transportation, technology chokepoints, critical infrastructure/cyber, financial-system stress, food/agriculture, domestic institutional stress, civil unrest/public order, public health/biological, and natural/environmental.
